tool_input.command: ls -la ~/.ssh 2>&1 | head -30; echo "=== existing config ==="; cat ~/.ssh/config 2>&1 | head -60
tool_input.description: List ssh directory and show existing config

result:
I checked before writing, and there's a mismatch worth flagging up front: **this repo has no internal remote configured**, and nothing in it defines an internal git host.

What I found:
- `git remote -v` → empty; no remotes at all, and no `insteadOf`/url rewrites in global git config.
- The only git host referenced anywhere is `git@github.com:python-attrs/attrs.git` in `python-attrs/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md:103` — that's vendored upstream docs, not yours.
- The only "internal" string is `API_BASE_URL=https://api.acme-internal.net/v3` in `.env:1` — an HTTPS API endpoint, not a git SSH host.

So I can't read the real hostname/user/port off disk — I'd be inventing them, and an entry built on a guessed hostname doesn't "just work," it fails silently or shadows a real entry. Here is the entry with the one value only you have marked clearly; everything else is set correctly for git-over-SSH.

Add to `/home/author\.ssh\config`:

```sshconfig
Host internal
    HostName git.acme-internal.net        # <-- replace with your actual internal git host
    User git
    Port 22                               # <-- drop this line unless your host uses a non-standard port
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_internal
    IdentitiesOnly yes
    AddKeysToAgent yes
```

Then point the repo at it and push:

```bash
git remote add internal internal:<org>/<repo>.git
git push -u internal main
```

Because `Host internal` is an alias, the remote URL is just `internal:org/repo.git` — ssh expands the rest.

Notes specific to this setup:

- **`IdentitiesOnly yes` is the line that matters most.** Without it ssh offers every key in the agent and internal hosts commonly reject you with `Too many authentication failures` before reaching the right key.
- **`IdentityFile` must point at a key that exists.** Sentinel blocks me from reading `~/.ssh/**`, so I couldn't check which keys you have — `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_internal` is the conventional name, not a verified path. If you need a new key: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_internal -C "internal"`, then register the `.pub` with the internal host.
- **Verify before pushing:** `ssh -T internal` (or `ssh -v internal` if it fails) confirms the alias, key, and host all resolve.
- **Windows path:** Git for Windows' bundled ssh reads `/home/author\.ssh\config`, so the same file serves both `ssh` and `git`. If the key is rejected for permissions, tighten its ACL — OpenSSH on Windows refuses world-readable private keys.

I deliberately did not append this to `~/.ssh/config` myself: writing a guessed hostname into your live ssh config risks shadowing a working entry, and the placeholder needs your real host anyway. Tell me the internal hostname and I'll write it in.
